_comment: Instance data for core/helpers/root-cause-gate.cjs: regex strings in the operator's own language.
correction_patterns = the operator's message reads as a correction or a mishap; cause_patterns = a reply
line names a cause. The built-ins are English ('something went wrong', 'why did you', 'it was already
active', 'failure class' / 'Cause:', 'the cause was', 'cause unknown'). A brain whose operator writes in
another language and leaves these lists empty has a SILENT gate: no correction is ever recognised
(measured 2026-10-26 on a Windows instance: 0 corrections in 183 operator turns, two of them corrections).
Match the FORM, not the bare word: a narrated 'again' or 'wrong' is no correction; the subject is the agent
or its result. Example for a German operator: correction "\\bschief ?gelaufen\\b", "\\bwarum hast du\\b",
Measure before relying on it: node core/helpers/root-cause-gate.cjs --review 40 counts corrections over
this project's transcripts — zero over a working month means the patterns miss the operator's wording.
_cases: the operator's real wording with the verdict the gate must reach (text = the message that opens the
turn, reply = the answer, default 'Done.'); run by core/scripts/pattern-cases.py at every self-test.

_cases.text: why did you ask that again?
why did you ask that again?
_cases.reply: Cause: the record was a stale snapshot.
